title: Scaling Synthetic Data Creation with 1,000,000,000 Personas

paper.authors: Ge, Scholak, Chan, Gao, Du, Jin, Yu, Zhang, Yu (Tencent AI Lab Seattle)
paper.repo_license: code MIT, data CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (README badges; no LICENSE file is committed)
paper.eval_harness_repo: https://github.com/openai/simple-evals (MIT, (c) 2024 OpenAI), commit 652c89d0ca9df547706735883097e9537d40dc47 (2026-04-22; shallow clone at external/repos/W4400222256/openai__simple-evals) - the paper's footnote 6 names this repo as its MATH evaluation protocol. The persona-hub repo itself contains NO evaluation code.
paper.other_artifacts: Hugging Face proj-persona/PersonaHub (200,000 personas preview + 370M elite personas, released 2025-02-18) and the six released synthetic sample files shipped in the repo: math.jsonl (50,000), reasoning.jsonl (50,000), instruction.jsonl (50,000), knowledge.jsonl (10,000), npc.jsonl (10,000), tool.jsonl (5,000), persona.jsonl (200,000).

dependence.note: For the claim targeted here the LLM is the subject (an accuracy measured on model answers), but it is a comparison baseline rather than the paper's contribution. The paper's CORE dependence is component-type: GPT-4 generates the 1.09M persona-driven math problems and gpt-4o generates their solutions, which is a one-billion-scale generation loop we deliberately do not target. Note that the paper's own live-model measurement (Table 1) sits on an unreleased test set, and its Table 2 GPT rows are transcribed from OpenAI's leaderboard - see blockers.

claim.statement: Evaluated with OpenAI's simple-evals protocol on the 5,000-problem MATH test set (out-of-distribution reference row for the paper's fine-tuned 7B model), gpt-4o-2024-05-13 scores 76.6% and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 scores 73.4% accuracy, i.e. the paper's Qwen2-7B fine-tuned on 1.07M persona-synthesised problems (64.9%) is beaten only by these two, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini Pro 1.5 and DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (Table 2).
claim.metric: MATH accuracy (%) = share of the 5,000 test problems whose extracted 'Answer: $ANSWER' line is judged equivalent to the reference answer by the simple-evals LLM equality checker (common.check_equality with EQUALITY_TEMPLATE); chain-of-thought, zero-shot, single sample per repeat.

table1_in_distribution_11_6k_pct.note: not re-runnable - the 11.6K synthetic test set is not released

claim.original_source: Table 2 (p. 9, 'Out-of-distribution evaluation on MATH'); footnote 6 = https://github.com/openai/simple-evals; Sec. 4.1.2 for the evaluation setup. Rows without an asterisk are stated to use OpenAI's evaluation method.
claim.provenance_warning: The four GPT rows of Table 2 match the openai/simple-evals README leaderboard verbatim (gpt-4o-2024-05-13 76.6, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 73.4, gpt-4-0125-preview 64.5, gpt-4-1106-preview 64.3), so the persona authors transcribed rather than measured them. Re-running this card tests OpenAI's published number using the paper's declared protocol; it does not test a measurement the persona authors made.

protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - Table 2 prints the dated snapshots gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09; no alias inference needed. The undated 'gpt-4o' in the repo's demo script and the undated 'GPT-4' used as the problem generator are a different (generation-side) usage and are not this card's arm.

params.params_source: simple-evals ChatCompletionSampler defaults (temperature=0.5, max_tokens=1024); the persona paper reports no generation parameters of its own
params.answer_extraction: regex ANSWER_PATTERN on the response, then check_equality(equality_checker, gold, extracted)

protocol.seeds_note: simple-evals' own CLI runs MATH with n_repeats = 10 (the MathEval class default is 16), so the published 76.6 is very likely a 10-repeat mean over 50,000 samples. This card budgets 3 repeats and records the deviation; the 3-repeat estimate is noisier than the original.
protocol.equality_checker: simple-evals instantiates ChatCompletionSampler(model='gpt-4-turbo-preview') for the fuzzy answer match. That alias is DEAD (it resolved to the retired 0125-preview), so the grader must be substituted - proposed: gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 with the unchanged EQUALITY_TEMPLATE, validated against a rule-based match on an agreement sample.
protocol.evaluation: simple-evals math_eval.MathEval + common.aggregate_results (accuracy, bootstrap_std over items)

artifacts.prompts_path: external harness: openai/simple-evals math_eval.py (QUERY_TEMPLATE) and common.py (EQUALITY_TEMPLATE). The persona-hub repo's own prompts (code/prompt_templates.py: math_template, instruction_template, knowledge_template, npc_template) are the DATA-GENERATION prompts, not the evaluation prompt.
artifacts.data_path: https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/simple-evals/math_test.csv (5,000 MATH test problems; math_500_test.csv is the 500-problem IID subset). Persona-hub's own released data: data/{math,reasoning,instruction,knowledge,npc,tool,persona}.jsonl
artifacts.eval_path: openai/simple-evals math_eval.py, common.py (check_equality, aggregate_results), simple_evals.py. persona-hub ships only code/openai_synthesize.py and code/vllm_synthesize.py (generation demos, model alias 'gpt-4o', temperature 0.7).
artifacts.data_license: MATH: MIT (Hendrycks et al.); simple-evals: MIT; persona-hub data: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; persona-hub code: MIT
artifacts.redistributable: MATH and simple-evals yes (MIT, attribution); persona-hub data non-commercial only
artifacts.notes: The released math.jsonl carries only {input persona, synthesized text} - the synthesised PROBLEMS with no solutions and no answers - so neither the 20K held-out set nor the 11.6K consistency-filtered test set of Table 1 can be reconstructed from the release. Repo size 253 MB (under the 1 GB cap); simple-evals is a few hundred KB.

blockers: Claim provenance: the Table 2 GPT rows are copied verbatim from the openai/simple-evals README leaderboard, not measured by the persona authors, so this card re-executes OpenAI's number under the paper's declared protocol rather than a persona-hub measurement. The user must accept that framing (see user_checks).

The paper's own live-model numbers (Table 1: gpt-4o 91.2, gpt-4-turbo 88.1) are on the 11.6K synthetic test set, which is not released and cannot be reconstructed - the released 50,000 math problems have no answers and are not identified as the held-out split.
The simple-evals equality checker is gpt-4-turbo-preview, a dead snapshot; any substitute grader changes the metric definition slightly and must be validated on an agreement sample.

Sampling-scheme mismatch: simple-evals runs MATH at n_repeats = 10 and temperature 0.5; our 3 repeats give a wider interval than the published figure, and the persona paper states neither parameter itself.
Cost: the full 5,000-item x 3-repeat protocol is ~$125 for the gpt-4o arm alone (~$250 more to add gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09), well above the low-cost band.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0); the top row of Table 2 and the paper's headline comparator

successors: gpt-5.6-sol (vendor-designated replacement for gpt-4o per the OpenAI deprecations page) and gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 (GPT-4-class comparator; its own leaderboard MATH value is 82.1)
arms.open_weight_anchor: Qwen2-7B-Instruct and Llama-3-70B-Instruct are Table 2 rows and can be hash-pinned; the paper's own fine-tuned Qwen2-7B checkpoint is NOT released, so the 64.9 row cannot be reproduced without redoing the fine-tune.

budget.assumptions: Subject pass: 5,000 items x 3 repeats = 15,000 calls, ~160 input tokens (70-token template + problem) and ~500 output tokens of step-by-step work under the 1,024 cap -> $12 in + $112.5 out = ~$125. Equality-checker pass: 15,000 calls at ~200 in / ~3 out with gpt-4.1-nano -> ~$0.3. Cheaper option: the 500-problem math_500_test split at 3 repeats costs ~$13 in total. Adding the gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 arm at 5,000 x 3 would add ~$250 at $10/$30 per 1M.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 MATH accuracy (median of 3 repeats) against 76.6%. Survival = the re-run accuracy falls inside the bootstrap 95% CI over the 5,000 items around 76.6% (about +/- 1.2 pp, widened for the 3-vs-10 repeat deviation) AND the ordering claim of Table 2 holds, i.e. gpt-4o > gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 > 64.9 (the paper's fine-tuned 7B). Partial = the level moves outside the CI but the ordering survives. Death = gpt-4o drops to or below 64.9, which would undo the paper's framing that its 7B model 'matches gpt-4-turbo-preview' while trailing the frontier. Report the grader-substitution sensitivity (dead gpt-4-turbo-preview vs gpt-4.1-nano) before any drift conclusion.
judgment.notes: Because the original figure is a transcribed leaderboard value, a mismatch is evidence about OpenAI's published MATH number under the current serving stack, not about the persona authors' pipeline. That distinction must be stated wherever this card's result is used.

user_checks: Accept the Table 2 MATH row (gpt-4o-2024-05-13 = 76.6) as this paper's claim even though the value is transcribed from OpenAI's simple-evals leaderboard, or drop the paper to 'no re-runnable own claim' (its own live-model rows are on the unreleased 11.6K set)?
Scope and cost: full MATH 5,000 at 3 repeats (~$125), or the official 500-problem math_500_test subset at 3 repeats (~$13) with the subsampling recorded as a deviation?
Equality checker: substitute gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 for the dead gpt-4-turbo-preview with the unchanged EQUALITY_TEMPLATE, and validate on a 300-item agreement sample?
Add the gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 arm (73.4) for ~$250, or keep this card single-arm?
domain_notes: The paper's contribution is a persona-driven data-synthesis pipeline (1B personas; 1.09M GPT-4-generated math problems with gpt-4o solutions) and a Qwen2-7B fine-tuned on 1.07M of them. Neither end of that pipeline is re-runnable here: the generation loop is orders of magnitude beyond any card budget, the fine-tuned checkpoint is not released, and the 20K/11.6K evaluation splits are not released (the public math.jsonl holds 50,000 problems without solutions or answers). What remains bounded and re-executable is the Table 2 reference row on the public MATH test set with a public MIT-licensed harness. The paper's only other bounded live-model number, the 20K -> 11.6K retention under two-of-three solution agreement (gpt-4o assistant, gpt-4o PoT, gpt-4-turbo assistant), would be an attractive card but neither the split nor the solution prompts are released. Quality of the synthesised problems was judged by two human math experts (7/200 invalid, 96.5% valid), which is a human outcome and out of scope.
